The `sanitize` method in `org.apache.commons.compress.utils.ArchiveUtils` takes a string input and removes any characters that are not ISO control characters or in the `SPECIALS` UnicodeBlock by replacing them with a question mark. This method is called in the failing test `sanitizeShortensString`.

Given the failing test `sanitizeShortensString`, which compares the sanitized output of a long input string, and the current bug report mentioning an issue with a problematic error message related to a truncated .zip-File, it seems likely that the error message in the current bug report is being generated using the sanitized output of a zip file content.

The sanitizer method replaces non-ISO control characters with a question mark. If the content of the truncated .zip-File contains non-ISO control characters, the sanitizer would replace them with question marks, potentially altering the content and leading to the error message being displayed incorrectly.

To confirm this hypothesis, we should investigate how the error message related to the truncated .zip-File is being generated and whether the santized content is involved in it.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
